text:
dan_arch: sketching a follow-up to the CP split RFC — proposing a "locality boundary" layer for egress connectors. gist: keep control plane auth/state global, but surface a per-region lightweight boundary that owns egress NAT/affinity and short-circuiting. thoughts?

alex_m: can you toss the sketch here? curious how this differs from the existing relay/peering options we already discussed.

dan_arch: pasted diagram below (ascii):
```
  global-cp
    |\n    +-- region-A-boundary --> tenant-egress-pool-A (ENI/NAT) --> internet / customer-vpc
    |\n    +-- region-B-boundary --> tenant-egress-pool-B
```
key idea: boundaries hold ephemeral egress leases, route affinity, and the minimal cert bundle. CP retains canonical metadata but does not own src-ip preservation.

priya_r: so boundaries act like thin operators — they don't terminate model traffic, just handle L3/4 egress and short-circuit to closest regional endpoints?

dan_arch: exactly. benefits: lower cross-region hairpin, better latency for regional customers, more predictable egress accounting.

jamal_s: what about identity? if the boundary holds certs, does that widen blast radius if a boundary is compromised? also how do we rotate?

dan_arch: good call. proposal: boundary has a short-lived signing key material (KMS-wrapped) pulled during bootstrap. CP issues signed lease tokens with TTL. rotate by renewing leases; boundary key rotation is local and audited to CP logs.

sara_ops: how does this affect private endpoint customers who require no outbound internet and only private peering?

dan_arch: for private-only customers boundary still exists but the egress-pool maps to a private endpoint (VPC peering or PrivateLink). The boundary enforces policy but doesn't perform NAT to the public internet. so same surface, different backend.

alex_m: what are failure/rollback semantics? if a boundary loses connectivity to CP do we fail open (best-effort) or closed?

dan_arch: recommend fail-soft: continue serving short-lived leases until TTL expires, but mark region degraded in console and stop creating new leases. if boundary is partitioned and auth fails on renewal, traffic continues until leases age out (default 10m).

priya_r: any measurable perf numbers? rough token-cost/regional-savings estimate?

dan_arch: quick sim: for 30% regional-local traffic we see ~25% lower p95 due to less cross-region hops and ~12% egress-cost delta because we avoid double-transit on relays. numbers need spike testing.

jamal_s: ops overhead concerns: more endpoints to rotate / monitor. do we centralize logs?

dan_arch: yes central S3/log pipeline with region-aware indices. boundary exposes health + lease metrics to CP and we run auto-remediation playbook (restart on cert mismatch, tombstone IPs on leak).

infra-bot: deploy-checklist v0.1 generated: [boundary image build], [lease protocol v2], [metrics export], [private-endpoint mapping], [cutover playbook].

sara_ops: rollout plan idea: feature-flag per-customer. start with dev tenants in region-A, run for 2 weeks, monitor p95, egress bill, and NAT exhaustion.

alex_m: what about compatibility with Dedicated/Private offerings where customers want full isolation?

dan_arch: Dedicated gets the boundary but deployed into customer-managed VPC (sidecar-mode). Private (airgapped) can run boundary with a stub CP sync over async connector. behavior and API same; implementation differs.

priya_r: security checklist items to add: IAM least-priv, KMS envelope separation, mTLS for CP<->boundary, signed lease token + nonce anti-replay.

jamal_s: also add integration test for route-flap during lease renewal — ensure no src-ip flip mid-connection.

dan_arch: noted. I'll iterate RFC appendix with: lease token format, TTL defaults, health signals, cutover playbook, and rollout gate metrics. action items:
- dan_arch: update appendix + diagram (due EOD Friday)
- priya_r: write security checklist (due Mon)
- jamal_s: test plan for NAT/route-flap (due next Wed)
- sara_ops: rollout playbook draft (due next Fri)

alex_m: :thumbsup: sounds reasonable. small nit: call it "locality boundary" in docs, not "edge boundary" to avoid product confusion.

dan_arch: agreed. will push draft to RFC repo and ping arch review. thanks all.
